Subject: SIG: request for reproducible noisy-neighbor test harness and artifacts

Lauren —

Thanks for taking SIG intake. Acme's security team needs concrete artifacts showing how Redwood Dedicated prevents cross-tenant interference for GPU-bound workloads. Specifically we are asking for:

- A short description of the reproducible noisy-neighbor test harness you use (steps, workload profiles, and expected outputs).
- Raw perf/NVML samples from a representative test run (1–2 minute window).
- Any pprof/flamegraphs showing CPU/GPU hotpaths during contention.
- A written summary that explains how isolation is enforced at the runtime/hypervisor/kernel level and what mitigations exist for evictions.

Requested delivery date: Fri 9 Oct 2026 (we have an internal review next week). If you can provide a link to a staging S3/Drive bundle with the artifacts and a 1–page README, that would be ideal.

Happy to clarify scope — we don't need production telemetry for customer data, just reproducible test outputs and docs.

Thanks,
Jenny Alvarez
Security Engineer, Acme Corp
[jenny.alvarez@acme-corp.com]

[Attachment: Acme_SIG_questions_20261005.pdf]

Lauren / Aditya —

We can deliver what they asked for. Quick plan:

1) Repro harness: a small orchestrator (python script) that launches two containers on the same GPU node:
   - victim: 1x Llama-like generation loop (static prompt), pinned to GPU 0, captures nvml/pid stats and samples at 250ms.
   - noisy: synthetic kernel (cuBLAS heavy matmul) running at a configurable intensity.
   - harness will run 90s by default and produce a README with steps and expected metrics.

2) Captures/artifacts:
   - NVML per-process samples (csv) for the window (nvml_samples.csv).
   - GPU utilization timelines (util_timeline.png).
   - pprof CPU profiles and flamegraphs for the victim (pprof_victim.pb, flame_victim.svg).
   - kernel logs when preemption/eviction happens (dmesg snippets).

3) Isolation explanation: short doc that covers: GPU driver namespaces we use, our allocation policy (exclusive GPU mode vs MPS), how KV cache eviction is handled, and eviction backoff strategy.

Notes / questions:
- Do we give them examples from Dedicated (reserved pools) or from a multi-tenant staging node? Better to run on a Dedicated test node to avoid customer data.
- I will anonymize hostnames and tune sampling to avoid PII.

I'll put the harness and outputs in staging S3 under the ACME folder and share the link. ETA for artifacts: Thu 8 Oct EOD internal (so Lauren we can send on Fri to Acme).

— Vivek
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
